channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: PL oficializa Portinho ao Senado pelo Rio
item.description: The PL officially announced on Friday, the 24th, the pre-candidacies of Douglas Ruas for governor of Rio de Janeiro and Carlos Portinho for the Federal Senate from the same state. Portinho emphasized the need for a Senate majority to overcome conflicts between branches of government, particularly with the STF, stating society can no longer tolerate the 'tug-of-war' between Judiciary and Executive. The announcement is part of the PL’s strategy to strengthen its base in Rio for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Álvaro Damião assume a presidência da federação União-PP em Minas
item.description: Belo Horizonte Mayor Álvaro Damião (União Brasil) assumed the presidency of the União Progressista Federation in Minas Gerais on July 23, with a mandate until December 31, 2029. He emphasized a commitment to a more developed, fraternal, and humane country, thanking national party leaders, especially Antônio Rueda of União Brasil. The federation also includes federal deputy Pinheirinho (PP) as vice-president and Ana Paula Junqueira (PP) as a titular member.

item.title: O gol de Lula em Flávio nos bastidores da pré-campanha eleitoral
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro struggles to attract Centrão support due to poor political articulation, having relied on last-minute deals that failed, according to José Benedito da Silva. In contrast, Lula has already built state-level electoral slates nationwide, pursuing a gradual, pragmatic strategy to keep dialogue open with center parties while prioritizing political space over early commitments. The União Brasil, PP, Republicanos, PSD, and MDB now focus on expanding congressional caucuses, avoiding premature alliances to remain relevant regardless of the election outcome.

item.title: Governo Lula 3 terá 31 leilões de rodovias até o fim do ano, diz ministro
item.description: Transport Minister George Santoro said the Lula 3 government will conduct 31 road concessions by the end of 2026, nearing the initial target of 35. He explained that new concession models feature greater risk-sharing and contractual predictability to attract investors amid high interest rates. Rail transport was also highlighted as a key mobility priority for the next decade.

item.title: Crises, disputas e reconciliações: os conflitos entre Michelle e filhos de Bolsonaro
item.description: The relationship between former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro and the sons of former President Jair Bolsonaro deteriorated over years, culminating in an open dispute within the family's political core. Tensions stem from disagreements over electoral strategy, public visibility, and influence within the Bolsonarist movement, as Michelle seeks greater political autonomy while the sons defend the traditional leadership of the clan.

item.title: Após pedido de Lula, Marcelo Ramos deixa disputa ao Senado no Amazonas
item.description: Marcelo Ramos (PT-AM) withdrew from the Senate race in Amazonas following a direct request from President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). His withdrawal clears the path for Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM) to become the sole center-left senatorial candidate, preventing vote splitting that could advantage right-wing candidates like Alberto Neto (PL-AM) and Wilson Lima (União Brasil). Ramos stated that, while he believed the PT should have a Senate candidate, he could not oppose the president, his political leader.

item.title: Governo prevê reduzir bloqueio em verbas de ministérios a R$17,9 bi em meio a redução de despesas obrigatórias
item.description: The Lula government announced it will reduce the budgetary block on ministries from R$23.7 billion to R$17.9 billion, due to lower-than-expected projections for mandatory spending on personnel, pensions, and social benefits. The adjustment aims to comply with the annual expenditure ceiling without imposing deeper cuts on sectoral programs.

item.title: Lula chama Bolsonaro de “imbecil” e diz que sua mente é “atrofiada”
item.description: Lula called Bolsonaro an "imbecile" and said his mind was "atrophied" during a visit to the Avibras Aeroco factory. He defended the BNDES's technical management, stating that Bolsonaro's criticisms were unfounded and highlighted the resumption of operations at the defense company.

item.title: Governo Lula reduz bloqueio de gastos e libera R$ 5,7 bilhões no Orçamento de 2026
item.description: The Lula government reduced budget blocking by R$ 5.7 billion, lowering it from R$ 23.7 billion to R$ 17.9 billion, according to the bimestral report from the Ministry of Planning. This release comes on the eve of the 2026 electoral campaign and reflects revised spending forecasts, with cuts in pension benefits, BPC, and personnel costs, offset by increases in health and unemployment insurance. The projected primary surplus for 2026 rose from R$ 4.1 billion to R$ 10.8 billion (after accounting adjustments), though the result without exceptions remains deficient at R$ 52 billion.

item.title: Nicarágua rebate Itamaraty e diz ter eleições “livres e transparentes”
item.description: Nicaragua responded to Brazil's criticisms, asserting that it continues to hold democratic, free, and transparent elections in defense of its national sovereignty. The statement from Nicaragua's Foreign Ministry was issued days after President Daniel Ortega declared he would not hold new elections to prevent the opposition from returning to power. The Brazilian government had expressed concern over Ortega's remarks, reiterating that free, periodic, plural, and transparent elections are fundamental pillars of democracy.

item.title: Foie gras proibido no Brasil: como o patê de fígado de ganso virou uma iguaria gastronômica?
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed law 15.475, banning the production and commercialization of foods obtained through forced animal feeding, including foie gras, making Brazil the second country in Latin America to implement such a ban after Argentina. The measure was celebrated by animal protection NGOs, including Animal Equality Brasil, which led a six-year campaign, crediting the victory to the engagement of thousands of supporters and collaboration with other animal welfare organizations.

item.title: INSS: Lula destina R$ 547 milhões para ressarcir descontos ilegais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva allocated R$ 547 million through MP 1.378/2026 to reimburse INSS beneficiaries who suffered illegal deductions from their benefits between 2019 and 2024, mainly due to unauthorized association fees. The fraud scheme, estimated at over R$ 6 billion, was exposed by Metrópoles and investigated by the Federal Police in Operation Sem Desconto, leading to the dismissal of the INSS president and Minister of Social Security Carlos Lupi. Although the deadline to request reimbursement ended on June 20, beneficiaries can still check eligibility via the Meu INSS portal or by calling 135.

item.title: Luisa Mell elogia e agradece Lula pela proibição do foie gras no Brasil
item.description: Influencer and activist Luisa Mell praised and thanked President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for signing Law No. 15.475, which bans the production, commercialization, and import of foie gras in Brazil. The law, set to take effect in 180 days, targets the force-feeding of ducks and geese, a practice condemned by animal protection groups as cruel. Luisa Mell commended the president’s courage and sensitivity, suggesting the decision could encourage other nations to adopt similar bans.

item.title: Empresa para a qual Flávio Bolsonaro emitiu R$ 1 milhão em notas não existe no endereço informado
item.description: The consulting firm Copenhagen, for which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s law office issued R$1 million in canceled invoices, does not physically exist at the address registered with the Federal Revenue in São Caetano do Sul. The premises are occupied solely by Contábil Corrêa, another company owned by the same individual, Rogério Lourenço Novo, who also received invoices from the senator. Copenhagen is under investigation by the Federal Police for suspected asset concealment in the Master case, and Bolsonaro has not clarified the nature of the legal services provided or how he met Novo.

item.title: O ping-pong da impunidade: quando o STF chama de diálogo o que é fraude ao diálogo
item.description: The STF upheld Constitutional Amendment 133/2024, allocating 30% of electoral funds to Black candidacies, but exempted parties from past non-compliance by labeling it 'refinancing' rather than amnesty. The ruling emphasizes institutional dialogue between branches, yet rewards prior violations, turning a constitutional duty into a post-hoc negotiation. Critics contend this legitimizes electoral fraud by conflating dialogue with accommodation, undermining anti-racist constitutional goals.

item.title: Caiado busca apoio na União-PP após federação negar palanque a Flávio
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) is seeking support from União Brasil and PP leaders after their federation declined to endorse Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the presidential race. The former governor of Goiás sees the federation’s neutrality as an opportunity to persuade state directories to join his campaign. The move reflects ongoing efforts to build strategic alliances ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Participação efetiva de Michelle na campanha de Flávio depende de trégua com Carlos, Eduardo e 'chihuahuas raivosos', dizem aliados
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro's participation in Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign hinges on a truce with brothers Carlos and Eduardo Bolsonaro, as well as managing radical supporter groups described as 'rabid chihuahuas'. While Flávio's public apology was seen as a positive first step, allies say the reconciliation will be gradual, requiring private talks after the PL convention, logistical adjustments, and family cooperation—including care for Jair Bolsonaro during her campaign travels.

item.title: A estratégia por trás do novo capítulo de Flávio e Michelle, segundo cientista político
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s public apology to Michelle Bolsonaro is a campaign strategy aimed at regaining support from women and evangelical voters, who have shown increasing resistance to the senator during the pre-campaign. According to political scientist Rafael Cortez, the reconciliation seeks to recover a base that had shifted toward blank or null votes following incidents like the Master case and audio leaks. Although there has been a slight recent rebound in polls, the overall trend remains a gradual decline in support since May.

item.title: Centrão vê Michelle com ‘passe mais caro’ e com intenções para emplacar vice
item.description: Centrão leaders assess that Michelle Bolsonaro increased her political value by managing the resolution of the crisis with Flávio Bolsonaro, showing willingness to play a decisive role in defining his presidential ticket. They believe she used the situation to her advantage to secure a public pardon and demonstrate her influence within the PL and among key voters, such as women and evangelicals. However, they do not see the reconciliation as a major turning point for Flávio’s campaign, which still depends on the end of public scandals and remains hostage to other challenges, including his ties to Daniel Vorcaro and the new tariff hike.

item.title: Lula defende Forças Armadas preparadas para ‘não deixar ninguém meter o nariz’ no Brasil
item.description: President Lula (PT) advocated for investment in well-equipped and prepared Armed Forces during a visit to Avibras Aeroco in Jacareí (SP), emphasizing the need to safeguard Brazil’s territorial sovereignty and deter foreign interference. He compared the military to God—something people may not believe in until they need it—stressing that preparedness ensures peace and national dignity, even as he reiterated his opposition to war.

item.title: Ao defender investimentos em defesa, Lula afirma que há ‘loucos pelo mundo querendo fazer guerra’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for increased investment in Brazil's Armed Forces, citing global threats of conflict and the country's natural wealth in critical minerals, forests, and freshwater. He referenced Brazil's extensive borders and historical invasions, such as the Paraguayan War, to justify military preparedness. Lula made these remarks during a visit to Avibras Aeroco in Jacareí, a defense company that resumed operations after a three-year workers' strike.

item.title: Crises, disputas e reconciliações: a cronologia dos conflitos entre Michelle e filhos de Bolsonaro
item.description: The relationship between Michelle Bolsonaro and the sons of former President Jair Bolsonaro deteriorated over the years, marked by protocol breaches at the 2019 inauguration, social media disconnections after 2022, and indirect exchanges in 2024, particularly involving Carlos Bolsonaro. The conflicts reflect disputes over political influence, space within the Liberal Party, and electoral strategies, with Michelle expressing feelings of disrespect from her stepsons. Despite public affirmations of unity, behind-the-scenes dynamics reveal a growing rift within the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que proíbe a venda e produção de foie gras
item.description: President Lula signed Law No. 15.475, banning the production and sale of foie gras in Brazil, a product obtained through force-feeding (gavagem), widely condemned as animal cruelty by global protection groups. The law imposes fines and potential imprisonment for violators, classifying offenses under environmental crimes law and possible animal mistreatment charges.

item.title: Flávio esnobou Ciro por causa de Vorcaro e, agora, fica sem PP e com PF
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro lost PP support after snubbing Ciro Gomes over Daniel Vorcaro, worsening his political standing. Despite still seeking the centrão for his 2026 candidacy, he faces challenges due to an audio linking him to multimillion demands and the nickname 'Tariflávio', compounded by Michelle Bolsonaro's explosive video. His behavior, inherited from his father, hinders a favorable comeback.

item.title: Tarcísio ameaça caducar contrato com Trivia Trens após falhas e incêndio
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas threatened to terminate the concession contract with Trivia Trens after a train fire on Line 12-Safira disrupted service between Brás and Tatuapé. Artesp temporarily returned operation of lines 11-Coral, 12-Safira and 13-Jade to CPTM for 90 days due to repeated operational failures by the concessionaire, which had only begun service on Monday.

item.title: Venda de spray de pimenta para mulheres é liberada; saiba as regras
item.description: The federal government sanctioned a law allowing the sale and possession of pepper spray for women aged 18 and over, vetoing provisions for teenagers aged 16 and the requirement to report loss or theft. The law sets technical standards, including a 50 ml limit on the requirement of will lead the of residence, and criminal background check requiring a self to confirm lack of convictions for violent crime.

item.title: Veto ao foie gras no Brasil reacende tensão comercial com a França após acordo Mercosul-UE
item.description: President Lula signed a law banning the production and commercialization of foie gras in Brazil, a move praised by animal rights groups but reigniting commercial tensions with France, the world's top producer of the delicacy, shortly after the Mercosul-EU trade agreement was signed.

item.title: Cards, tweets e vídeos: Flávio Bolsonaro aposta em site para militantes com conteúdos contra Lula
item.description: The PL launched the 'Direita Já' platform to register influencers and distribute ready-made content (cards, tweets, videos) against Lula, with daily updates and a partner program. Flávio Bolsonaro promoted the site in a live stream, claiming it combats 'many lies' and will be a reference in the 2026 elections. The PT previously adopted a similar strategy in 2023 with 'influencers with Lula' and in 2025 with 'pode espalhar'.

item.title: JOTA entrevista na segunda (27/7) Wolney Queiroz, ministro da Previdência Social
item.description: Minister of Social Security Wolney Queiroz will be interviewed by JOTA on Monday (July 27) at 5 p.m. to discuss the consigned credit landscape, potential reductions in INSS interest rate caps, and the future of Brazil’s pension system amid population aging, gig work, and outsourced labor. The interview takes place amid market and societal anticipation of Lula’s economic plan for a possible new term and future pension reforms.

item.title: Flávio resgata fala de Lula sobre roubo de celulares e promete penas mais duras
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) revived a statement by President Lula about youths involved in cellphone thefts to accuse the government of being lenient toward criminals. In a social media video, the pre-candidates for president promised to toughen penalties for crimes such as cellphone robbery. Published on Friday, the 24th, the post reinforces the senator’s opposition strategy against the federal government.

item.title: Flávio diz que vai fazer “tesouraço em tudo que atrasa o Brasil”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, stated that if elected, he would implement a 'tesouraço' on everything delaying Brazil, promising lower taxes, less bureaucracy, and greater government efficiency. He criticized President Lula as having outdated ideas, being tired and lacking modernity, and linked the PT to corruption. Flávio will be officially launched as a candidate on Saturday (July 25) in São Paulo.

item.title: Mesmo sem ofensiva do Planalto, Republicanos acena para neutralidade na corrida presidencial
item.description: The Republicanos party has opted for neutrality in the 2026 presidential election, having not been approached by the Lula government to prevent support for Flávio Bolsonaro — unlike PP and União Brasil. Internal resistance to backing Bolsonaro’s son, combined with challenges in forming state-level alliances with the PL, is driving the party’s decision to stay out of the presidential race. This stance underscores the party’s independence from both Planalto negotiations and the bolsonarist candidacy.

item.title: Podemos discutir uma reforma de previdência no setor público, diz Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated the federal government intends to discuss and support spending containment measures, particularly targeting public pension expenditures in the Judiciary and Armed Forces, citing monthly pensions of up to R$ 400,000 as unsustainable. He noted that Brazil’s gross public debt rose from 71% of GDP in 2023 to 81% in May 2026, with the IMF projecting 100% of GDP by 2027, and that the government aims to stabilize this metric between 2029 and 2030 through cuts to mandatory spending.

item.title: Eleição no Rio: Douglas Ruas larga sem vice e tenta se descolar de Cláudio Castro
item.description: Douglas Ruas, president of the Alerj, was officially nominated as the PL's candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro in a ticket currently without a running mate after Rogerio Lisboa withdrew. He aims to distance himself from former governor Cláudio Castro and center his campaign on public safety, seeking to link Eduardo Paes (PSD) to Lula's unpopular PT government in the state.

item.title: Brasileiras já podem comprar spray de pimenta para defesa pessoal
item.description: Starting this Friday, Brazilian women over 18 with no criminal record for violent or serious threat crimes can purchase pepper spray for self-defense, requiring ID and proof of residence. The law, signed by President Lula, bans containers over 50 ml and limits use to legitimate defense situations, mandating proportional and moderate application. Lula vetoed provisions allowing minors to buy it with parental consent and specific penalties for misuse, which now fall under general assault and bodily injury laws.

item.title: Caiado busca apoio de aliados do PP e União, seu ex-partido, após federação declarar neutralidade
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado of the PSD said he will seek individual support from allies in the União Brasil and PP federation, despite their declared neutrality in the 2026 presidential election. He emphasized his political history with these parties and plans to persuade leaders personally. The neutrality allows state directories to choose candidates freely, with the PP already aligned with Flávio Bolsonaro in São Paulo and Lula in Paraíba.

item.title: Crusoé: “Votar em Flávio é estender tapete para esquerda”
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, pre-candidate for president from the PSD, stated on social media that voting for Flávio Dino rolls out the red carpet for the left, warning of the risk of strengthening the left if Dino is elected. Caiado added that Lula, despite having been president three times, never managed to form a lasting political consensus. His candidacy will be formalized at a PSD convention in São Paulo on Sunday, January 26.

item.title: Tarifaço dos EUA: setores veem risco para economia e pedem ao governo que insista no diálogo em vez de agir com reciprocidade
item.description: The Brazilian government announced it will initiate procedures to apply the Reciprocity Law in response to new U.S. tariffs of 25% and 12.5%, deemed arbitrary. Business associations such as Abimaq, Amcham, and CNI advocated for dialogue over retaliation, warning of the risk of commercial escalation and its economic impacts.

item.title: As ações do PT para afastar o Centrão de Flávio
item.description: The PT worked to keep the PP-União Brazil federation neutral in the presidential race, negotiating with leaders like José Guimarães, Edinho Silva, Lula, and Camilo Santana to prevent support for Flávio Bolsonaro and preserve future government cooperation. Flávio Bolsonaro planned a gesture for Michelle Bolsonaro at the PL convention and received symbolic backing from Javier Milei, while Michelle aims to stay low-profile, focusing on her Senate campaign and Jair Bolsonaro’s. Meanwhile, the U.S. imposed new tariffs on up to 37.5% of Brazilian products, drawing international criticism as unfounded.

item.title: Candidata do Novo em SP ficou R$ 4,3 milhões mais rica em dois anos
item.description: Maria Helena, Novo party candidate for federal deputy in 2026 and former São Paulo mayoral candidate in 2024, declared to the TSE that her wealth increased by R$ 4.3 million between 2024 and 2026, rising from R$ 9.7 million to R$ 14 million. The growth stemmed from purchasing a new R$ 1.35 million house (replacing a R$ 381,000 apartment) and increasing investments from R$ 1.7 million to R$ 5.1 million. Her asset declarations from 2020 and 2022 were later removed from the TSE platform at her request, citing personal information.

item.title: Moraes revoga medidas cautelares contra Márcio Canella
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes revoked the precautionary measures imposed on former Belford Roxo mayor Márcio Canella, including electronic ankle monitor, nighttime and weekend house arrest, passport surrender, and periodic court appearances. The decision was made on July 22, 2026, following his arrest in the 6th phase of Operation Unha e Carne, during which a military-style rifle and other weapons were seized. Moraes stated there is no evidence to infer the crime of illegal firearm possession, as the seized weapons appear to be duly registered and safeguarded by military police officers.

item.title: Dr. Furlan venceria no 1º turno no AP, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll released on July 24, 2026, shows that former Macapá mayor Dr. Furlan (PSD) would win the Amapá gubernatorial election in the first round with 66% of voting intentions, compared to 30% for incumbent governor Clécio Luís (União Brasil). The survey, conducted among 1,600 voters from July 19–23, has a 95% confidence level and a 2-point margin of error, and was registered with the TSE under AP-02970/2026. It cost R$24,000.00 and was self-funded.

item.title: Douglas Ruas é oficializado candidato ao governo do Rio pelo PL, critica governo Castro e nacionaliza discurso
item.description: Douglas Ruas was officially nominated as the PL candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro at a party convention, criticizing the Cláudio Castro government for poor performance in education, security, and employment. He nationalized his discourse by linking Eduardo Paes to President Lula, warning against creating a 'PT bunker' in the state. The ticket still lacks a vice-presidential candidate after Rogério Lisboa's withdrawal, and a Senate seat remains pending.

item.title: STF terá segundo tempo da disputa pelo orçamento
item.description: The STF is set to revisit the conflict between the Executive and Legislative branches over budget control, four years after the initial clashes over the 'secret budget.' The court's ruling on the CVM demonstrates that the Judiciary is already acting to counter side effects of budget opacity, such as legislative encroachment on regulatory agency appointments. The secret budget, allocating R$ 50 billion annually in amendments, undermines governability and oversight, prompting investigations into resource diversions and hindering nominations to oversight bodies.

item.title: Prisão de aliado de Flávio Bolsonaro no Rio sofre reviravolta no STF
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes revoked precautionary measures against Márcio Canella, former mayor of Belford Roxo, after confirming the rifle found with him was registered to a military police officer providing his escort. Canella, a Senate pre-candidate on a ticket with Douglas Ruas (PL) and backed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, had been arrested in flagrante during Operation Unha e Carne, which investigates a money laundering scheme using gas stations in Rio’s metropolitan area, involving R$ 7.6 billion over six years.

item.title: Lula é aprovado por 50% e desaprovado por 48% no AP, diz pesquisa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's administration is approved by 50% and disapproved by 48% of voters in Amapá, according to a Real Time Big Data survey conducted from July 19 to 23, 2026. The government's evaluation shows 36% rating it as 'excellent' or 'good', 29% as 'fair', and 34% as 'poor' or 'terrible'. The poll interviewed 1,600 voters, has a 2-point margin of error, and is registered with the TSE under BR-05542/2026.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas tem apoio de PSDB e Cidadania em SP
item.description: The PSDB-Cidadania federation in São Paulo confirmed its support for the re-election of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) in the 2026 elections, a decision to be ratified at the state convention on July 28. At the same event, the federation will launch its majoritarian Senate candidacy, with Soninha Francine (Cidadania) as the lead candidate. The endorsement keeps the race for São Paulo governor focused on Tarcísio and Fernando Haddad (PT), who was announced as a pre-candidate in March.

item.title: Zema avalia que governo foi passivo diante de ameaça tarifária dos EUA: 'Lula ficou quieto'
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's pre-candidate, criticized the Lula government for being passive in the face of new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports, which now stand at 12.5% following a Section 301 investigation into alleged forced labor practices. He argued that Lula prioritized rapprochement with anti-American nations like Venezuela, Cuba, and Iran, distancing Brazil from its second-largest trading partner, the U.S. Zema also supported renegotiating Rio Grande do Sul's debt with the Union and proposed splitting Petrobras to introduce competition, opposing traditional privatization.

item.title: Tarcísio quer receber Milei com tapete azul no Palácio dos Bandeirantes
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas plans to receive Argentine President Javier Milei with a blue carpet at the Palácio dos Bandeirantes, instead of the traditional red one, this Saturday (25). The symbolic choice of blue aligns with the visual identity of the São Paulo state government and reflects an ideological gesture of proximity to the libertarian Argentine leader. The meeting takes place amid efforts to strengthen ties between Brazilian subnational governments and foreign leaders aligned with market-oriented agendas.

item.title: Após destaque no Girona, Vitor Reis volta ao Manchester City em busca de espaço
item.description: Vitor Reis returned to Manchester City after a standout season on loan at Girona, where he started 37 of 38 matches and led the team in defensive clearances. His performances earned him a call-up to the Brazil national team ahead of the 2026 World Cup. He is now competing for a place in Enzo Maresca's squad during the club's preseason tour in Asia.
